iterations.theme: Sustavni slom hrvatske poljoprivrede i status poljoprivredne kolonije

sections.subtitle: Uvod: Propast hrvatske poljoprivrede – tema od nacionalne važnosti
sections.screenshot_description: Voditeljica predstavlja Milana Medića, stručnjaka za ruralni razvoj, u studiju podcasta Mrežnica.
sections.content: Podcast Mrežnica otvara goruću temu hrvatske poljoprivrede, postavljajući ključna pitanja: **kada, zašto i kako je propala?** Voditeljica ističe kako je dugo tražila sugovornika koji neće 'filozofirati', već će ponuditi konkretne uvide iz prakse. Kao idealan izbor predstavljen je gospodin Milan Medić, dugogodišnji stručnjak za ruralni razvoj, predsjednik Lider mreže Hrvatske i voditelj lokalne akcijske grupe Valisko Lapis. Medić, poznat po svom terenskom radu i izravnom pristupu, odmah na početku naglašava da poljoprivreda, iako nije jedina djelatnost, predstavlja **najvažniju gospodarsku granu za ruralna područja**. Bez funkcionalne poljoprivrede, druge grane poput turizma ili poduzetništva ne mogu nadoknaditi ekonomske tokove u ruralnim zajednicama, što je, kako ističe, očigledan problem u Hrvatskoj.
sections.subtitle_en: Introduction: The collapse of Croatian agriculture – a topic of national importance
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host introduces Milan Medić, an expert for rural development, in the studio of the Mrežnica podcast.
sections.content_en: The Mrežnica podcast opens the burning topic of Croatian agriculture, posing key questions: **when, why, and how did it fail?** The host points out that she searched for a long time for an interlocutor who would not 'philosophize', but would instead offer concrete insights from practice. Presented as the ideal choice is Mr. Milan Medić, a long-time expert in rural development, president of the Lider mreža Hrvatske, and leader of the local action group Valisko Lapis. Medić, known for his field work and direct approach, emphasizes right at the beginning that agriculture, although not the only activity, represents **the most important economic branch for rural areas**. Without functional agriculture, other branches like tourism or entrepreneurship cannot compensate for the economic flows in rural communities, which is, as he points out, an obvious problem in Hrvatska.

sections.subtitle: Sustavno uništenje otkupa: Ključni uzrok propasti sela
sections.screenshot_description: Milan Medić objašnjava kako je uništenje sustava otkupa dovelo do urušavanja sela.
sections.content: Gospodin Medić iznosi svoju temeljnu tezu: **Hrvatska je upropastila i uništila sustav otkupa primarnih poljoprivrednih sirovina.** Konkretno, u Hrvatskoj se gotovo više ne otkupljuje mlijeko od seljaka, nema organiziranog otkupa teladi i odojaka, a mesna industrija ne proizvodi finalne proizvode iz hrvatskih sirovina. Onog trenutka kada u selu prestane otkup mlijeka, mesa i ostalih primarnih poljoprivrednih proizvoda, dolazi do potpunog urušavanja sela. Ovaj problem ima i dramatične demografske posljedice; Hrvatska je u 35 godina samostalnosti izgubila čak 20% stanovništva, što je milijun ljudi. Voditeljica dodaje kako se često misli da je dovoljno imati hranu, no ona je uglavnom uvozna – mrkva i peršin iz Italije, krumpir iz Egipta, mladi luk iz Srbije – što ukazuje na dubinu problema.
sections.subtitle_en: Systematic destruction of purchasing: The key cause of the ruin of the village
sections.screenshot_description_en: Milan Medić explains how the destruction of the purchase system led to the collapse of the village.
sections.content_en: Mr. Medić presents his fundamental thesis: **Hrvatska has ruined and destroyed the system of purchasing primary agricultural raw materials.** Specifically, in Hrvatska, milk is almost no longer purchased from peasants, there is no organized purchase of calves and piglets, and the meat industry does not produce final products from raw materials from Hrvatska. The moment the purchase of milk, meat, and other primary agricultural products stops in the village, a complete collapse of the village occurs. This problem also has dramatic demographic consequences; Hrvatska has, in 35 years of independence, lost as much as 20% of its population, which is a million people. The host adds how it is often thought that it is enough to have food, but it is mostly imported – carrots and parsley from Italija, potatoes from Egipat, spring onions from Srbija – which points to the depth of the problem.

sections.subtitle: Kronologija sloma: Od industrije do poljoprivrede
sections.screenshot_description: Grafički prikaz pada broja proizvođača mlijeka u Karlovačkoj županiji.
sections.content: Propast hrvatske poljoprivrede nije se dogodila preko noći, već se razvijala desetljećima. Milan Medić objašnjava da je proces započeo uništavanjem industrije kroz **kriminalnu privatizaciju** u devedesetima, da bi se u dvijetisućitima prešlo na sustavno uništavanje poljoprivrede. Kao drastičan primjer navodi Karlovačku županiju, gdje je 2000. godine bilo 300 organiziranih proizvođača mlijeka, dok ih je prošle godine bilo samo 10 – pad od nevjerojatnih 97%. Slična je situacija i na nacionalnoj razini; bjelovarska mljekara Sirela je osamdesetih godina imala 45.000 kooperanata, dok danas cijela Hrvatska broji tek 2.500 do 3.000 organiziranih proizvođača mlijeka. Medić ovu situaciju naziva **nacionalnom katastrofom** i pitanjem nacionalne sigurnosti, a ne samo poljoprivrede.
sections.subtitle_en: Chronology of the collapse: From industry to agriculture
sections.screenshot_description_en: Graphical representation of the decline in the number of milk producers in Karlovac County.
sections.content_en: The collapse of Croatian agriculture did not happen overnight, but developed over decades. Milan Medić explains that the process began with the destruction of industry through **criminal privatization** in the nineties, only to transition to the systematic destruction of agriculture in the two-thousands. As a drastic example, he cites Karlovac County, where in the year 2000 there were 300 organized milk producers, while last year there were only 10 – a drop of an incredible 97%. A similar situation is also at the national level; the Bjelovar dairy Sirela had 45,000 subcontractors in the eighties, while today the whole of Croatia counts only 2,500 to 3,000 organized milk producers. Medić calls this situation a **national catastrophe** and a matter of national security, and not just of agriculture.

sections.subtitle: Tko je kriv i prvi znakovi urušavanja sustava
sections.screenshot_description: Prikaz natpisa 'prodajem' na seoskim ogradama, simbolizirajući neorganiziranu prodaju.
sections.content: Za propast poljoprivrede Milan Medić izravno krivi **sve Vlade koje su vodile državu u posljednjih 25 do 30 godina**, ne isključujući ni aktualnu. Kritizira i bivšeg premijera Milanovića, koji je nedavno govorio o važnosti samodostatnosti u proizvodnji hrane, pitajući se što je radio dok je bio premijer s ministrom poljoprivrede Jakovinom. Prvi pokazatelji uništene poljoprivrede vidljivi su na selima, gdje se na ogradama i plotovima nižu natpisi 'prodajem mlijeko', 'prodajem janjce', 'prodajem med'. Takva neorganizirana prodaja, ističe Medić, nezamisliva je u uređenim zemljama poput Austrije, Njemačke ili Italije, i jasan je znak **potpunog sloma sustava**. Nadalje, hrvatska prehrambena industrija, poput karlovačke PPK industrije i Gavrilovića, danas ima nula kooperanata i svoje poslovanje temelji na kupovini sirovina s burze, uglavnom iz uvoza, što je dovelo do napuštanja sustava njegovanja domaće primarne proizvodnje.
sections.subtitle_en: Who is to blame and the first signs of the collapse of the system
sections.screenshot_description_en: Display of the sign 'for sale' on village fences, symbolizing unorganized sale.
sections.content_en: For the collapse of agriculture, Milan Medić directly blames **all Governments that have led the state in the last 25 to 30 years**, not excluding even the current one. He also criticizes former Prime Minister Milanović, who recently spoke about the importance of self-sufficiency in food production, wondering what he was doing while he was Prime Minister with the Minister of Agriculture Jakovina. The first indicators of destroyed agriculture are visible in villages, where signs 'I sell milk', 'I sell lambs', 'I sell honey' line up on fences and wooden fences. Such unorganized sale, Medić points out, is unthinkable in well-ordered countries like Austrija, Njemačka or Italija, and is a clear sign of **the complete collapse of the system**. Furthermore, the Croatian food industry, like the karlovačka PPK industrija and Gavrilović, today has zero cooperators and bases its business on buying raw materials from the stock exchange, mostly from imports, which has led to the abandonment of the system of nurturing domestic primary production.

sections.subtitle: Liberalizacija uvoza i EU pregovori: Cijena ulaska u Uniju
sections.screenshot_description: Grafikon koji prikazuje smanjenje kvota za poljoprivrednu proizvodnju tijekom EU pregovora.
sections.content: Milan Medić identificira dva ključna trenda koja su dovela do propasti poljoprivrede. Prvi je **proces pridruživanja Europskoj uniji**, tijekom kojeg je Hrvatska, kako navodi, bitno smanjivala svoje kvote za proizvodnju. Spominje dokument Ministarstva vanjskih poslova (koji je u međuvremenu uklonjen s weba) koji je detaljno prikazivao pregovore, gdje je Hrvatska pristajala na znatno manje kvote od početno predloženih. Drugi, i po njemu veći problem, je **potpuna liberalizacija uvoza** koju su dopustile hrvatske Vlade. Medić naglašava da nijedna ozbiljna država ne dopušta takvu liberalizaciju, nazivajući 'slobodno tržište' ideološkom floskulom za 'kolonijalne zemlje'. Uspoređuje to s praksom u Austriji i Italiji, gdje poljoprivreda funkcionira planski, kroz zadruge s dugoročnim ugovorima. Kao primjer navodi njemačku tvrtku koja je, unatoč dobroj berbi jabuka u Hrvatskoj, prvo morala otkupiti cjelokupnu njemačku proizvodnju, dokazujući to ministarstvu, prije nego što je mogla uvoziti. To pokazuje kako ozbiljne države štite svoju domaću proizvodnju, dok Hrvatska to nije činila.
sections.subtitle_en: Liberalization of imports and EU negotiations: The price of entry into the Union
sections.screenshot_description_en: A graph showing the reduction of quotas for agricultural production during the EU negotiations.
sections.content_en: Milan Medić identifies two key trends that led to the ruin of agriculture. The first is the **process of joining the European Union**, during which Croatia, as he states, significantly reduced its production quotas. He mentions a document of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (which has in the meantime been removed from the web) that detailed the negotiations, where Croatia agreed to significantly smaller quotas than those initially proposed. The second, and according to him bigger problem, is the **complete liberalization of imports** allowed by Croatian Governments. Medić emphasizes that no serious state allows such liberalization, calling the 'free market' an ideological platitude for 'colonial countries'. He compares this with the practice in Austria and Italy, where agriculture functions in a planned manner, through cooperatives with long-term contracts. As an example, he mentions a German company which, despite a good apple harvest in Croatia, first had to buy up the entire German production, proving this to the ministry, before it could import. This shows how serious states protect their domestic production, while Croatia did not do so.

sections.subtitle: Poljoprivreda kao pitanje nacionalne sigurnosti: Hrvatska 'turistička zemlja'?
sections.screenshot_description: Milan Medić gestikulira, naglašavajući važnost poljoprivrede za nacionalnu sigurnost.
sections.content: Milan Medić snažno ponavlja da je **poljoprivreda pitanje nacionalne sigurnosti**, a ne samo ekonomska grana. Izražava frustraciju što ministri poljoprivrede i premijeri ne razumiju ovu ključnu činjenicu, sugerirajući da bi sigurnosne službe poput SOA-e trebale alarmirati politički vrh. Voditeljica se nadovezuje na često ponavljanu tezu da je 'Hrvatska turistička zemlja' i da će živjeti od turizma i EU fondova, dok se poljoprivreda zanemaruje. Medić citira kolegu Nevena Bidakovića, koji ističe da Hrvatska može biti turistička zemlja, ali ne smije zanemariti industriju i poljoprivredu. Upozorava na opasnost oslanjanja isključivo na turizam, pitajući se što će se dogoditi ako turizam zakaže, a zemlja nema dovoljno hrane ni za vlastite potrebe.
sections.subtitle_en: Agriculture as a question of national security: Croatia a 'tourist country'?
sections.screenshot_description_en: Milan Medić gesticulates, emphasizing the importance of agriculture for national security.
sections.content_en: Milan Medić strongly repeats that **agriculture is a question of national security**, and not just an economic branch. He expresses frustration that ministers of agriculture and prime ministers do not understand this key fact, suggesting that security services like SOA should alarm the political leadership. The host builds on the frequently repeated thesis that 'Hrvatska is a tourist country' and that it will live off tourism and EU funds, while agriculture is neglected. Medić quotes colleague Neven Bidaković, who points out that Hrvatska can be a tourist country, but must not neglect industry and agriculture. He warns of the danger of relying exclusively on tourism, wondering what will happen if tourism fails, and the country does not have enough food even for its own needs.

sections.subtitle: 7 milijardi eura i pad proizvodnje: Financiranje propasti
sections.screenshot_description: Prikaz izvještaja Državne revizije s podacima o ulaganjima i padu proizvodnje.
sections.content: Gospodin Medić iznosi šokantne podatke iz najnovijeg izvještaja Državne revizije (ožujak 2024.). Hrvatska je u razdoblju od 2014. do 2028. godine imala na raspolaganju **7 milijardi eura** za ruralni razvoj. Unatoč tome što je već oko 4 milijarde eura uloženo, **realna vrijednost poljoprivredne proizvodnje u Hrvatskoj pala je za 25%** u odnosu na 2010. godinu. Medić to naziva 'financiranjem pada' i 'bacanjem novca'. Objašnjava ovaj apsurd primjenom **Okamove britve**: najjednostavnije objašnjenje je da je uništen sustav otkupa primarnih poljoprivrednih proizvoda. Ulaganje u mehanizaciju poput traktora i kombajna je besmisleno ako seljaci nemaju kome prodati svoje proizvode. Koristi metaforu broda: ako je 'kobilica' (organizirani otkup) probijena, brod tone bez obzira na 'palubu i kabine' (mehanizaciju i ulaganja).
sections.subtitle_en: 7 billion euros and the fall of production: Financing of ruin
sections.screenshot_description_en: Presentation of the State Audit report with data on investments and the decline in production.
sections.content_en: Mr. Medić presents shocking data from the latest report of the State Audit (March 2024). Croatia had at its disposal **7 billion euros** for rural development in the period from 2014 to 2028. Despite the fact that about 4 billion euros has already been invested, **the real value of agricultural production in Croatia fell by 25%** compared to the year 2010. Medić calls this 'financing of the decline' and 'throwing away money'. He explains this absurdity by applying **Occam's razor**: the simplest explanation is that the system of purchase of primary agricultural products has been destroyed. Investing in machinery like tractors and combines is pointless if farmers have no one to sell their products to. He uses the metaphor of a ship: if the 'keel' (organized purchase) is breached, the ship sinks regardless of the 'deck and cabins' (machinery and investments).

sections.subtitle: Usporedba s Jugoslavijom i primjer Lactalisa: Različiti pristupi privatizaciji
sections.screenshot_description: Prikaz logotipa Lactalisa i Dukata, simbolizirajući promjene u prehrambenoj industriji.
sections.content: Uspoređujući današnju situaciju s razdobljem Jugoslavije, Milan Medić ističe da je bivša država bila srednje razvijena industrijska zemlja, izvozno orijentirana, koja je sustav organiziranog otkupa razvijala desetljećima uz značajno sufinanciranje države. Primjeri poput Sirele s 45.000 kooperanata i KIM-a s preko 1.000 u osamdesetima svjedoče o razvijenosti sustava. Hrvatska prehrambena industrija, poput Podravke, bila je izuzetno razvijena i samostalna. Medić navodi primjer **Lactalisa**, francuske mljekarske industrije, koja je istovremeno kupila hrvatske tvrtke KIM i Dukat te talijansku Parmalat. Dok je u Hrvatskoj Lactalis promijenio poslovnu politiku, prešavši na uvoz mlijeka i smanjenje domaće proizvodnje, u Italiji to nije učinio. Parmalat i dalje otkupljuje mlijeko od tisuća talijanskih proizvođača. Medić zaključuje da Italija, kao ozbiljna država, nije dopustila promjenu poslovnog modela koja bi uništila domaću proizvodnju, što ukazuje na **nedostatak ozbiljnosti hrvatske države**.
sections.subtitle_en: Comparison with Yugoslavia and the example of Lactalis: Different approaches to privatization
sections.screenshot_description_en: Display of the logos of Lactalis and Dukat, symbolizing changes in the food industry.
sections.content_en: Comparing today's situation with the period of Jugoslavija, Milan Medić points out that the former state was a medium-developed industrial country, export-oriented, which developed a system of organized purchase for decades with significant state co-financing. Examples like Sirela with 45,000 cooperators and KIM with over 1,000 in the eighties testify to the development of the system. The Croatian food industry, like Podravka, was extremely developed and independent. Medić cites the example of **Lactalis**, a French dairy industry, which simultaneously bought the Croatian companies KIM and Dukat as well as the Italian Parmalat. While in Hrvatska Lactalis changed its business policy, switching to the import of milk and the reduction of domestic production, in Italija it did not do so. Parmalat still purchases milk from thousands of Italian producers. Medić concludes that Italija, as a serious state, did not allow a change in the business model that would destroy domestic production, which points to a **lack of seriousness of the Croatian state**.

sections.subtitle: Zašto se ulaže, a proizvodnja pada? Pitanje nacionalne sigurnosti
sections.screenshot_description: Milan Medić objašnjava kako uvoz sirovina utječe na kvalitetu proizvoda i gospodarstvo.
sections.content: Na pitanje voditeljice je li Hrvatska 'neozbiljna država', Milan Medić potvrđuje da se tako čini. Ponavlja da je to **pitanje nacionalne sigurnosti** i da se u državi mora voditi briga o tome. Ističe da se u Hrvatskoj ulaže mnogo novca u poljoprivredu, ali proizvodnja i dalje pada. Objašnjava da taj novac, umjesto da ostaje u zemlji, odlazi van, primjerice za kupnju talijanskih ili njemačkih traktora. Medić odbacuje argument da se ljudi ne žele udruživati u zadruge zbog 'socijalizma', tvrdeći da bi se udružili kada bi imali siguran otkup. Naglašava prednosti domaće proizvodnje: **kontrola kvalitete** (podsjeća da je hrvatska mesna industrija u Jugoslaviji imala NATO licence), novac ostaje u državi, samodostatnost i izvoz. Kritizira praksu uvoza 'smeća od sirovina' (zaleđeno meso iz vojnih rezervi, GMO proizvodi) od kojih se ne može proizvesti kvalitetan finalni proizvod.
sections.subtitle_en: Why is investment being made, and production is falling? A question of national security
sections.screenshot_description_en: Milan Medić explains how the import of raw materials affects the quality of products and the economy.
sections.content_en: To the presenter's question whether Croatia is an 'unserious state', Milan Medić confirms that it seems so. He repeats that this is a **question of national security** and that care must be taken about it in the state. He points out that in Croatia a lot of money is invested in agriculture, but production still falls. He explains that this money, instead of staying in the country, goes outside, for example for the purchase of Italian or German tractors. Medić rejects the argument that people do not want to associate into cooperatives because of 'socialism', claiming that they would associate if they had secure purchase. He emphasizes the advantages of domestic production: **quality control** (he reminds that the Croatian meat industry in Yugoslavia had NATO licenses), money remains in the state, self-sufficiency and export. He criticizes the practice of importing 'garbage of raw materials' (frozen meat from military reserves, GMO products) from which a quality final product cannot be produced.

sections.subtitle: Hrvatska kao 'banana država' i poljoprivredna kolonija
sections.screenshot_description: Karta Europe s označenim 'banana državama' i poljoprivrednim velesilama.
sections.content: Voditeljica spominje Dolinu Neretve, koja bi mogla hraniti pola države, a ostaje neobrađena, pitajući se je li to rezultat 'pranja mozga', snishodljivosti prema EU ili lijenosti. Milan Medić ponovno ističe **liberalizaciju uvoza** kao glavni uzrok, za koju su odgovorne sve dosadašnje Vlade. Smatra da uvozni lobiji postoje, ali da ih država dopušta. Poziva se na izvještaj Državne revizije koji pokazuje da je pad poljoprivredne proizvodnje, osim u Hrvatskoj, zabilježen samo u Rumunjskoj, Malti i Bugarskoj. Te zemlje naziva **'banana državama' jugoistoka Europe**, koje se oslanjaju na turizam i usluge, dok uvoze hranu. U isto vrijeme, prosječan rast poljoprivredne proizvodnje na europskoj razini iznosi 13%, što znači da su ozbiljne poljoprivredne velesile poput Italije, Francuske, Poljske, Njemačke i Austrije ostvarile značajan rast, štiteći svoju domaću proizvodnju. Medić zaključuje da država mora koristiti 'mrkvu i batinu' kako bi usmjerila razvoj poljoprivrede.
sections.subtitle_en: Hrvatska as a 'banana state' and an agricultural colony
sections.screenshot_description_en: Map of Europe with marked 'banana republics' and agricultural superpowers.
sections.content_en: The host mentions Dolina Neretve, which could feed half of the country, but remains uncultivated, wondering if this is the result of 'brainwashing', subservience to the EU, or laziness. Milan Medić again highlights **import liberalization** as the main cause, for which all previous Governments are responsible. He believes that import lobbies exist, but that the state allows them. He refers to the report of the Državna revizija which shows that the decline in agricultural production, except in Croatia, was recorded only in Romania, Malta, and Bulgaria. He calls these countries **'banana states' of Southeast Europe**, which rely on tourism and services, while importing food. At the same time, the average growth of agricultural production at the European level is 13%, which means that serious agricultural superpowers like Italy, France, Poland, Germany, and Austria achieved significant growth, protecting their domestic production. Medić concludes that the state must use 'carrot and stick' to direct the development of agriculture.

sections.subtitle: Novac od EU fondova odlazi iz Hrvatske: Kolonijalni model
sections.screenshot_description: Prikaz novca koji 'curi' iz Hrvatske, simbolizirajući odlazak EU fondova.
sections.content: Milan Medić naglašava da se **7 milijardi eura** iz EU fondova, namijenjenih hrvatskoj poljoprivredi, zapravo vraća u industrijske zemlje. Kao primjer navodi kupnju talijanskih ili njemačkih traktora umjesto nekadašnjih domaćih proizvoda poput Tomo Vinkovića. Hrvatska se, prema njegovim riječima, pozicionira kao **poljoprivredna kolonija**, gdje novac samo 'prolazi' kroz zemlju. Potkrepljuje to podacima Državne revizije o samodostatnosti: Hrvatska proizvodi 280% uljarica i 151% žitarica (višak), ali samo 62% mesa (deficit). To znači da **Hrvatska izvozi sirovine** (uljarice i žitarice za stočnu hranu) i **uvozi gotove proizvode** (meso). Ovaj model, gdje dodana vrijednost ostaje vani, a Hrvatska financira tuđu proizvodnju, klasičan je primjer kolonijalnog odnosa. Medić to uspoređuje s izvozom trupaca i uvozom gotovih kuhinja, što uništava domaću industriju.
sections.subtitle_en: Money from EU funds is leaving Croatia: A colonial model
sections.screenshot_description_en: Depiction of money which 'leaks' from Hrvatska, symbolizing the departure of EU funds.
sections.content_en: Milan Medić emphasizes that **7 billion euros** from EU funds, intended for Croatian agriculture, is actually returning to industrial countries. As an example, he cites the purchase of Italian or German tractors instead of former domestic products like Tomo Vinković. Croatia, according to his words, is positioning itself as an **agricultural colony**, where money only 'passes' through the country. He supports this with data from the State Audit on self-sufficiency: Croatia produces 280% of oilseeds and 151% of cereals (surplus), but only 62% of meat (deficit). This means that **Croatia exports raw materials** (oilseeds and cereals for animal feed) and **imports finished products** (meat). This model, where the added value remains outside, and Croatia finances someone else's production, is a classic example of a colonial relationship. Medić compares this to the export of logs and the import of finished kitchens, which destroys the domestic industry.

sections.subtitle: 'Game Over' za hrvatsku poljoprivredu: Što zapravo jedemo?
sections.screenshot_description: Milan Medić objašnjava drastičan pad poljoprivredne proizvodnje i postavlja pitanje kvalitete hrane koju konzumiramo.
sections.content: Gospodin Milan Medić, stručnjak za ruralni razvoj, alarmantno konstatira da je hrvatska poljoprivreda dosegla točku 'game over'. Ističe da je proizvodnja mlijeka u Karlovačkoj županiji pala za nevjerojatnih 97%, s 360 organiziranih proizvođača 2000. godine na samo 110 prošle godine. Slična je situacija i s primarnom proizvodnjom mesa, koja je također doživjela pad od preko 90%. Medić se pita što Hrvati zapravo jedu i piju, navodeći primjer kamiona mlijeka u prahu koji se razmoči i proda kao svježe mlijeko, dok se domaće mlijeko otkupljuje u malim količinama ili se od njega proizvode sirevi za izvoz. Naglašava da ovakav drastičan pad proizvodnje nije samo ekonomski problem, već nacionalna katastrofa i pitanje nacionalne sigurnosti.
sections.subtitle_en: 'Game Over' for Croatian agriculture: What are we actually eating?
sections.screenshot_description_en: Milan Medić explains the drastic decline of agricultural production and poses the question of the quality of food that we consume.
sections.content_en: Mr. Milan Medić, an expert in rural development, alarmingly states that Croatian agriculture has reached the 'game over' point. He points out that milk production in Karlovačka županija has fallen by an incredible 97%, from 360 organized producers in the year 2000 to only 110 last year. The situation is similar with primary meat production, which has also experienced a decline of over 90%. Medić wonders what Croatians actually eat and drink, citing the example of trucks of powdered milk that is reconstituted and sold as fresh milk, while domestic milk is purchased in small quantities or cheeses for export are produced from it. He emphasizes that such a drastic decline in production is not only an economic problem, but a national catastrophe and a matter of national security.

sections.subtitle: Demografski slom i ograničena uloga LAG-ova
sections.screenshot_description: Milan Medić govori o povezanosti propasti poljoprivrede i demografskog gubitka, te o ulozi lokalnih akcijskih grupa.
sections.content: Propast poljoprivrede usko je povezana s demografskim slomom Hrvatske. Milan Medić upozorava da je Hrvatska u 35 godina samostalnosti izgubila 20% stanovništva, što je 'demografski gubitak' koji se može usporediti sa samoubojstvom nacije. U kontekstu oporavka, Medić kritički promatra ulogu Lokalnih akcijskih grupa (LAG-ova), ističući da one raspolažu s tek 5% sredstava programa ruralnog razvoja. Preostalih 95% budžeta, prema njegovim riječima, troši se 'bez veze' jer je 'kobilica broda probijena', odnosno temeljni sustav organiziranog otkupa primarnih poljoprivrednih sirovina je uništen. Bez tog temelja, sva ulaganja u 'farbanje palube i jedara' su uzaludna jer brod i dalje tone.
sections.subtitle_en: Demographic collapse and the limited role of LAGs
sections.screenshot_description_en: Milan Medić speaks about the connection between the collapse of agriculture and demographic loss, and about the role of local action groups.
sections.content_en: The ruin of agriculture is closely connected with the demographic collapse of Croatia. Milan Medić warns that Croatia has, in 35 years of independence, lost 20% of its population, which is a 'demographic loss' that can be compared to the suicide of a nation. In the context of recovery, Medić critically observes the role of Local Action Groups (LAGs), pointing out that they dispose of only 5% of the funds of the rural development program. The remaining 95% of the budget, according to his words, is spent 'pointlessly' because 'the keel of the ship is pierced', that is, the fundamental system of organized purchase of primary agricultural raw materials is destroyed. Without that foundation, all investments in 'painting the deck and sails' are in vain because the ship still sinks.

sections.subtitle: Svjetli primjeri: Sirana Milka i inicijativa Karlovačke županije
sections.screenshot_description: Prikaz sirane Milka kao uspješnog modela i inicijative Karlovačke županije za lokalni otkup hrane.
sections.content: Unatoč sumornoj slici, postoje i pozitivni primjeri. Milan Medić ističe Siranu Milka iz Duge Rese, malu tvrtku s pet zaposlenih, koja ima 22 kooperanta. To znači da 22 obitelji žive od prodaje mlijeka ovoj lokalnoj sirani, što je, prema Mediću, društveni učinak usporediv s velikim mljekarama poput Kima, Vindije i Dukata u Karlovačkoj županiji, koje u prosjeku imaju tek oko 30 kooperanata. Medić također hvali Karlovačku županiju koja je, prepoznajući problem, uvela sustav lokalnog otkupa hrane za osnovne škole i vrtiće. Ova inicijativa, koja se planira proširiti na bolnice i staračke domove, služi kao primjer dobre prakse kako se političkom voljom može pokrenuti oporavak poljoprivrede na lokalnoj razini.
sections.subtitle_en: Bright examples: Sirana Milka and the initiative of Karlovačka County
sections.screenshot_description_en: Presentation of the Milka cheese factory as a successful model and the initiative of Karlovačka županija for local food purchase.
sections.content_en: Despite the gloomy picture, there are also positive examples. Milan Medić highlights Sirana Milka from Duga Resa, a small company with five employees, which has 22 cooperators. This means that 22 families live from the sale of milk to this local cheese factory, which is, according to Medić, a social impact comparable to large dairies like Kim, Vindija, and Dukat in Karlovačka županija, which on average have only about 30 cooperators. Medić also praises Karlovačka županija which, recognizing the problem, introduced a system of local food purchase for elementary schools and kindergartens. This initiative, which is planned to be expanded to hospitals and retirement homes, serves as an example of good practice of how the recovery of agriculture at the local level can be started by political will.

sections.subtitle: Nedostatak strateškog planiranja i put prema oporavku
sections.screenshot_description: Milan Medić objašnjava zašto je ključno strateško planiranje na državnoj razini i koliko bi trebalo za oporavak.
sections.content: Voditeljica postavlja pitanje zašto na državnoj razini nedostaje strateško planiranje, uspoređujući situaciju s Izraelom i Iranom koji, unatoč nedostatku vode i ratnim sukobima, imaju razvijenu poljoprivredu. Milan Medić ponavlja svoju 'Okamovu britvu' – najjednostavnije objašnjenje je najispravnije: problem je u uništenom sustavu otkupa primarnih poljoprivrednih proizvoda. 'Onog trenutka kad je Laktofriz otišao iz sela, ugasile su se štale. Onog trenutka kad su se ugasile štale, izumrlo je ruralno stanovništvo', objašnjava Medić. Procjenjuje da bi za ponovno uspostavljanje i razvoj tog sustava bilo potrebno 10 do 15 godina ozbiljnih državnih ulaganja, uz podršku banaka i praćenje seljaka. Iako je već 'debelo prekasno', Medić naglašava da je nužno početi odmah.
sections.subtitle_en: Lack of strategic planning and the path towards recovery
sections.screenshot_description_en: Milan Medić explains why strategic planning at the state level is crucial and how much time would be needed for recovery.
sections.content_en: The host poses the question of why strategic planning is lacking at the state level, comparing the situation with Israel and Iran which, despite the lack of water and war conflicts, have developed agriculture. Milan Medić repeats his 'Occam's razor' – the simplest explanation is the most correct: the problem is in the destroyed system of purchase of primary agricultural products. 'The moment Laktofriz left the village, the barns shut down. The moment the barns shut down, the rural population died out', Medić explains. He estimates that for the re-establishment and development of that system, 10 to 15 years of serious state investments would be necessary, with the support of banks and the following of peasants. Although it is already 'way too late', Medić emphasizes that it is necessary to start immediately.

sections.subtitle: Ministarstvo poljoprivrede: Nedostatak razumijevanja i povijesne usporedbe
sections.screenshot_description: Milan Medić izražava frustraciju zbog nerazumijevanja u Ministarstvu poljoprivrede i uspoređuje ga s prijašnjim sustavom.
sections.content: Milan Medić izražava frustraciju zbog nedostatka razumijevanja u Ministarstvu poljoprivrede i drugim ministarstvima. Iako priznaju problem, ne poduzimaju konkretne korake. Medić uspoređuje današnju situaciju s Republikom Socijalističkom Hrvatskom, gdje je Republički sekretarijat za poljoprivredu s 95 zaposlenih (uključujući čistačice) uspješno razvijao poljoprivredu. Danas, Ministarstvo poljoprivrede i Agencija za plaćanja zapošljavaju između 500 i 1000 ljudi, a realna poljoprivredna proizvodnja pala je za 25%. Medić zaključuje da je temeljni problem u nedostatku organiziranog otkupa primarnih poljoprivrednih proizvoda. Da taj sustav postoji, sve ostalo bi došlo kao dodatak i imalo bi smisla, poput kupovine traktora ili udruživanja u zadruge.
sections.subtitle_en: Ministry of Agriculture: Lack of understanding and historical comparisons
sections.screenshot_description_en: Milan Medić expresses frustration due to the lack of understanding in the Ministry of Agriculture and compares it with the previous system.
sections.content_en: Milan Medić expresses frustration because of the lack of understanding in the Ministarstvo poljoprivrede and other ministries. Although they recognize the problem, they do not take concrete steps. Medić compares today's situation with the Republika Socijalistička Hrvatska, where the Republički sekretarijat za poljoprivredu with 95 employees (including cleaning ladies) successfully developed agriculture. Today, the Ministarstvo poljoprivrede and the Agencija za plaćanja employ between 500 and 1000 people, and real agricultural production has fallen by 25%. Medić concludes that the fundamental problem is in the lack of organized purchase of primary agricultural products. If that system existed, everything else would come as an addition and would make sense, like buying tractors or joining cooperatives.

sections.subtitle: Povijest i značaj zadrugarstva: Od 19. stoljeća do danas
sections.screenshot_description: Milan Medić objašnjava dugu povijest zadrugarstva u Hrvatskoj, demistificirajući njegovu povezanost s Jugoslavijom.
sections.content: Milan Medić demistificira percepciju zadrugarstva kao relikta socijalizma, objašnjavajući da njegova povijest u Hrvatskoj seže u 19. stoljeće. Nakon ukidanja kmetstva 1848. godine, mali oslobođeni kmetovi morali su se udruživati u zadruge kako bi opstali uz velike posjede. Dalmacija je bila predvodnik u razvoju zadrugarstva. Iako je Jugoslavija u početku (1945.-1948.) napravila pogrešku s modelom kolhoza, brzo je odustala od njega i razvila sustav gdje je lokalna prehrambena industrija otkupljivala lokalne sirovine, često putem velikih zadruga. Medić naglašava da je to bio 'smisleni krug' koji je osiguravao stabilnost i razvoj. Danas, seljaci bi se udružili u zadruge ako bi im to donosilo profit, bez obzira na ideološke predrasude, ali problem je što industrija više ne bazira svoje poslovanje na domaćoj sirovini.
sections.subtitle_en: History and significance of cooperativism: From the 19th century to today
sections.screenshot_description_en: Milan Medić explains the long history of cooperativism in Hrvatska, demystifying its connection with Jugoslavija.
sections.content_en: Milan Medić demystifies the perception of cooperativism as a relic of socialism, explaining that its history in Hrvatska reaches back to the 19th century. After the abolition of serfdom in 1848, small freed serfs had to associate into cooperatives in order to survive alongside large estates. Dalmacija was a leader in the development of cooperativism. Although Jugoslavija in the beginning (1945-1948) made a mistake with the kolkhoz model, it quickly gave up on it and developed a system where the local food industry purchased local raw materials, often through large cooperatives. Medić emphasizes that this was a 'meaningful circle' that ensured stability and development. Today, farmers would associate into cooperatives if it brought them profit, regardless of ideological prejudices, but the problem is that the industry no longer bases its business on domestic raw materials.

sections.subtitle: Organizirani otkup: Temelj opstanka i put iz 'nule'
sections.screenshot_description: Milan Medić ponavlja ključnu ulogu organiziranog otkupa i potrebu za državnom intervencijom.
sections.content: Milan Medić ponovno ističe da je organizirani otkup primarnih poljoprivrednih proizvoda glavna osovina i temelj cijelog sustava. Kada mljekara 'hoće i mora' otkupljivati lokalno proizvedeno mlijeko, a mesna industrija lokalne bikove i odojke, tada se stvara osnova za razvoj zadrugarstva i cjelokupnog potpornog sustava. Hrvatska se, prema Mediću, vratila na 'nulu' u tom pogledu, a povratak je skup i dugotrajan. S obzirom na to da je prehrambena industrija danas uglavnom privatna, država mora djelovati u partnerstvu s vlasnicima, koristeći 'mrkvu i batinu' kako bi ih potaknula na promjenu poslovne politike i ponovno uspostavljanje otkupa domaće sirovine.
sections.subtitle_en: Organized buyout: The foundation of survival and the path from 'zero'
sections.screenshot_description_en: Milan Medić repeats the key role of organized purchase and the need for state intervention.
sections.content_en: Milan Medić points out again that the organized purchase of primary agricultural products is the main axis and foundation of the entire system. When a dairy 'wants and must' purchase locally produced milk, and the meat industry local bulls and piglets, then the basis for the development of cooperativism and the entire support system is created. Hrvatska, according to Medić, has returned to 'zero' in this regard, and the return is expensive and long-lasting. Considering that the food industry today is mostly private, the state must act in partnership with the owners, using 'carrot and stick' to encourage them to change business policy and re-establish the purchase of domestic raw materials.

sections.subtitle: Oportunizam u EU pregovorima i nedostatak strateških ciljeva
sections.screenshot_description: Milan Medić kritizira hrvatske vlade zbog oportunizma u EU pregovorima i nedostatka jasnih strateških ciljeva.
sections.content: Milan Medić kritizira hrvatske vlade zbog 'državnog oportunizma' tijekom pregovora za ulazak u Europsku uniju. Objašnjava da su tadašnje vlade pristale na znatno smanjene kvote za poljoprivrednu proizvodnju, što je dovelo do nepovoljnog položaja. Veći problem od samog oportunizma je, prema Mediću, nedostatak jasnih strateških ciljeva. Hrvatskim vladama je ulazak u EU bio cilj sam po sebi, bez definiranih koristi koje su željele postići za zemlju. To je rezultiralo posljedicama poput masovnog iseljavanja. Medić naglašava da je sada, u kontekstu globalnih kriza, ključno iskoristiti trenutak za strateško razmišljanje o osiguravanju hrane i opstanku ruralnog stanovništva.
sections.subtitle_en: Opportunism in EU negotiations and lack of strategic goals
sections.screenshot_description_en: Milan Medić criticizes Croatian governments for opportunism in EU negotiations and a lack of clear strategic goals.
sections.content_en: Milan Medić criticizes Croatian governments for 'state opportunism' during negotiations for entry into the European Union. He explains that the governments of that time agreed to significantly reduced quotas for agricultural production, which led to an unfavorable position. A bigger problem than opportunism itself is, according to Medić, the lack of clear strategic goals. For Croatian governments, entry into the EU was a goal in itself, without defined benefits that they wanted to achieve for the country. This resulted in consequences such as mass emigration. Medić emphasizes that now, in the context of global crises, it is crucial to use the moment for strategic thinking about securing food and the survival of the rural population.

sections.subtitle: Birokracija i rascjepkanost zemlje: Izgovori, a ne odgovori
sections.screenshot_description: Milan Medić objašnjava kako politička volja može nadvladati birokraciju i demantira izgovor o rascjepkanosti zemlje.
sections.content: Milan Medić odbacuje uobičajene izgovore za neuspjeh poljoprivrede, poput birokracije i rascjepkanosti zemljišta. Koristi analogiju s dva zupčanika: manji zupčanik je politika, a veći je državna birokracija. Ako politika ne 'zakurbla' u željenom smjeru i ne da strateško usmjerenje, birokracija će ostati neaktivna. 'Ako meni nitko ozgo šta se kaže nije dao direktivu, ja čitam sportske ili gloriju već šta tko voli i čekam tri da idem doma', slikovito objašnjava Medić. Argument o rascjepkanosti zemlje također smatra izgovorom, jer druge zemlje s istim problemom uspijevaju organizirati poljoprivrednu proizvodnju. Ključ je u političkoj volji koja mora dati jasne smjernice i koristiti 'mrkvu i batinu' za provedbu.
sections.subtitle_en: Bureaucracy and fragmentation of the country: Excuses, not answers
sections.screenshot_description_en: Milan Medić explains how political will can overcome bureaucracy and refutes the excuse about the fragmentation of the country.
sections.content_en: Milan Medić rejects common excuses for the failure of agriculture, such as bureaucracy and land fragmentation. He uses an analogy with two gears: the smaller gear is politics, and the larger is the state bureaucracy. If politics does not 'crank' in the desired direction and does not give strategic direction, the bureaucracy will remain inactive. 'If no one from above, as they say, has given me a directive, I read sports or Gloria, or whatever one likes, and wait for three to go home,' Medić explains vividly. He also considers the argument about land fragmentation to be an excuse, because other countries with the same problem manage to organize agricultural production. The key is in political will, which must give clear guidelines and use 'carrot and stick' for implementation.

sections.subtitle: Karlovačka županija kao model: Politička volja pokreće promjene
sections.screenshot_description: Milan Medić ponovno ističe Karlovačku županiju kao primjer kako politička volja može brzo pokrenuti promjene u poljoprivredi.
sections.content: Karlovačka županija ponovno služi kao najbolji primjer kako politička volja može pokrenuti promjene. Milan Medić objašnjava da je izravna politička volja županice dovela do uvođenja zelene javne nabave i sustava lokalnog otkupa hrane. Lokalni akcijski grupe i županijska razvojna agencija odmah su se prilagodile, dajući dodatne bodove poljoprivrednicima koji se jave na njihove natječaje i sudjeluju u ovom sustavu. U roku od tri do šest mjeseci postavljeni su temelji na kojima se dalje gradi. Medić ističe da ovaj model Karlovačke županije može služiti kao primjer cijeloj Hrvatskoj, pokazujući da administracija brzo reagira kada dobije jasnu direktivu od političkog vodstva.
sections.subtitle_en: Karlovačka County as a model: Political will drives changes
sections.screenshot_description_en: Milan Medić again points out Karlovačka županija as an example of how political will can quickly initiate changes in agriculture.
sections.content_en: Karlovačka županija again serves as the best example of how political will can initiate changes. Milan Medić explains that the direct political will of the county prefect led to the introduction of green public procurement and a system of local food purchase. Local action groups and the county development agency immediately adapted, giving additional points to farmers who apply to their tenders and participate in this system. Within three to six months, the foundations on which further building is done were set. Medić emphasizes that this model of Karlovačka županija can serve as an example to the whole of Croatia, showing that the administration reacts quickly when it receives a clear directive from the political leadership.

sections.subtitle: Zaključak: Nema uspješne zemlje s lošom poljoprivredom
sections.screenshot_description: Milan Medić zaključuje razgovor naglašavajući da je poljoprivreda temelj svake uspješne zemlje.
sections.content: Zaključujući razgovor, Milan Medić ponavlja da je hrvatska poljoprivreda na 'nuli'. Rješenje vidi u ponovnom uspostavljanju organiziranog otkupa primarnih poljoprivrednih sirovina – mlijeka, mesa, voća i povrća. Iako Podravka, jedna od najvećih europskih prehrambenih industrija, pokušava otkupljivati lokalno, to je zanemarivo u usporedbi s jugoslavenskim razdobljem, a velik dio sirovina i dalje uvozi. Medić naglašava da netko mora 'presjeći' takvu praksu i reći da se to više ne smije događati. Postavlja retoričko pitanje: 'Ima li uspješne zemlje koja ima lošu poljoprivredu?' i odgovara: 'Nema. Poljoprivreda je temelj svake industrije, svakog gospodarstva.'
sections.subtitle_en: Conclusion: There is no successful country with poor agriculture
sections.screenshot_description_en: Milan Medić concludes the conversation, emphasizing that agriculture is the foundation of every successful country.
sections.content_en: Concluding the conversation, Milan Medić repeats that Croatian agriculture is at 'zero'. He sees the solution in the re-establishment of organized purchase of primary agricultural raw materials – milk, meat, fruits and vegetables. Although Podravka, one of the largest European food industries, tries to purchase locally, this is negligible compared to the Yugoslav period, and it still imports a large part of the raw materials. Medić emphasizes that someone must 'cut' such practice and say that this must no longer happen. He poses a rhetorical question: 'Is there a successful country that has bad agriculture?' and answers: 'There is not. Agriculture is the foundation of every industry, of every economy.'

iterations.theme_en: Consequences of the collapse, local initiatives and the path towards recovery
